name: Arthur Purves
current_role: President of the Fairfax County Taxpayers Alliance
bio: Arthur Purves is a retired computer programmer who grew up in Washington, D.C., and has lived in Vienna, Virginia, since 1976. He holds degrees from the University of Pennsylvania and has led the Fairfax County Taxpayers Alliance for nearly three decades. He has run for office several times before.

platform.point: Reduce federal deficits by lowering demand for government services through better policy rather than eliminating programs.
Cut ultra-processed foods from diets to prevent chronic disease and lower government medical spending.
Oppose abortion except in rare cases where the mother's life is at risk.
Promote phonics instruction, the Core Knowledge curriculum and school vouchers to create competition.
Oppose carbon taxes and carbon regulations.
Display the Ten Commandments in public schools.

economy.evidence: Calls for lower taxes and cutting the roughly $2 trillion annual federal deficit and opposes Obamacare.

welfare.evidence: Opposes Obamacare but says spending can be cut without eliminating programs, mainly by improving nutrition.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion except to save the mother's life (community norms) while opposing complex gun laws (individual choice).

immigration.evidence: Wants immigrants vetted before entry to keep out traffickers and gang members.

energy.evidence: Opposes carbon taxes and regulations and criticizes California's energy policies.

education.evidence: Supports school vouchers to create competition and dropping Family Life Education programs.

faith.evidence: Supports placing the Ten Commandments in public schools.

name: Dianne Blais
bio: Dianne Blais is a longtime Northern Virginia community volunteer who has been active in the League of Women Voters and served as co-president of Virginia AAUW from 2008 to 2010. She was the Green Party nominee for Virginia's 10th District in 2014, an independent candidate for the House of Delegates in 2011, and a previous candidate in the 11th District.
notes: No 2026 campaign website or issue statements were found; earlier Green Party material describes her as anti-war and pro-environment, but the source page could not be loaded to confirm specifics.

name: Suzan DelBene
bio: Suzan DelBene has represented Washington's 1st District since 2012, serves on the Ways and Means Committee and chairs the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee. Before Congress she was a Microsoft executive, co-founded drugstore.com, led Nimble Technology and directed the Washington State Department of Revenue. She grew up partly in the Seattle area and studied at Reed College and the University of Washington.

platform.point: Protect the Affordable Care Act and work toward universal coverage with public and private options.
Pass the Women's Health Protection Act to guarantee abortion access nationwide.
Take near-term action on climate change, citing impacts already felt in the Pacific Northwest.
Pursue comprehensive immigration reform and legal limits on ICE enforcement tactics.
Prevent government and companies from gaining broad access to personal financial and health data.
Oppose dismantling the Department of Education and protect federal funding for public schools.

economy.evidence: Supports the Buffett rule so millionaires pay higher tax rates.

welfare.evidence: Backs the ACA and universal coverage with public and private options.

liberty.evidence: Supports nationwide abortion access and LGBTQ rights (individual choice), with background checks on all gun sales.

security.evidence: Backed ending bulk data collection under the PATRIOT Act while supporting community policing.

immigration.evidence: Supports legal status for DREAMers, higher visa caps and comprehensive reform.

foreign.evidence: Lists support for Ukraine and holding Putin accountable as an official priority, while requiring congressional approval for action against Iran.

tech.evidence: Advocates federal digital privacy protections and sponsored the Email Privacy Act.

education.evidence: Opposes voucher programs and supports public school funding.

name: Mary Silva
bio: Mary Silva is the Republican nominee for Washington's 1st Congressional District. Her campaign focuses on domestic tech manufacturing, national security, fiscal accountability and privacy. Little additional biographical information was found.

platform.point: Bring semiconductor manufacturing home, reform H-1B visas to favor American workers and expand apprenticeships.
Tighten border and clearance security and investigate foreign penetration of critical infrastructure.
Conduct a full Pentagon audit and cut intelligence contractor costs.
Require voter ID and create a midweek voting holiday.
Protect informed consent and parents' authority over children's health care.
End warrantless mass surveillance and enforce Fourth Amendment limits on data collection.

security.evidence: Calls for ending warrantless mass surveillance and banning foreign-linked police technology.

immigration.evidence: Wants stronger border security and H-1B reform prioritizing American workers.

notes: No professional background was found on the campaign site.

name: Rick Larsen
bio: Rick Larsen has represented Washington's 2nd District since 2001 and has been the top Democrat on the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee since 2023. He previously served on the Snohomish County Council and worked in public affairs for the Washington State Dental Association. He is from Arlington, Washington, and studied at Pacific Lutheran University and the University of Minnesota.

platform.point: Oppose broad tariffs and lower utility bills through clean energy.
Support universal, affordable coverage, drug price negotiation and a $35 monthly insulin cap.
Require ICE training standards, visible ID and body cameras, and end private detention facilities.
Raise the federal minimum wage to $17 an hour and expand affordable childcare.
Codify abortion rights in federal law.
Secure federal funding for roads, bridges, transit and aviation.

economy.evidence: Supports a 30% minimum tax on incomes over $1 million and a $17 federal minimum wage.

welfare.evidence: Supports universal, affordable coverage and expanded Medicare benefits.

liberty.evidence: Rated 100% by NARAL on abortion rights; supports background checks on all gun sales though rated B- by the NRA.

security.evidence: Voted against extending PATRIOT Act roving wiretaps.

immigration.evidence: Supports a path to citizenship and calls for ICE accountability and an end to private detention.

foreign.evidence: Co-chairs the APEC Caucus and Arctic Working Group and voted for Iraq war funding, though he opposed the 2002 authorization.

energy.evidence: Rated 95% by the League of Conservation Voters and voted for 2009 cap-and-trade.

education.evidence: Opposes school vouchers and is rated 100% by the NEA.

notes: Foreign policy evidence is mixed: OnTheIssues describes a preference for restraint, while his record includes war funding votes.

name: Edwin H. Feller
current_role: Construction trades contractor and business founder
bio: Edwin H. Feller grew up on a family farm in Lynden, Washington, and graduated from Lynden Christian High School in 1960. He spent much of his career overseas in construction trades work for U.S. government contractors and founded Feller Heating & Air Conditioning. The 2026 race is his first run for public office.

platform.point: Support strong law enforcement, designate cartels as terrorist organizations and end sanctuary policies.
Expand nuclear and hydroelectric power and scale back environmental mandates.
Define sex in Title IX as biological sex to protect female athletes.
Overhaul immigration with a merit-based points system that prioritizes nuclear families.

liberty.evidence: Wants Title IX to define sex as biological sex (LGBTQ issues); no stated positions found on other liberty issues.

security.evidence: Calls for robust law enforcement and treating cartels as foreign terrorist organizations.

immigration.evidence: Supports ending sanctuary policies and a merit-based points system.

energy.evidence: Backs expanded nuclear and hydro power while reducing environmental mandates.

notes: Positions come from local news coverage because the campaign site shows little policy content.

name: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez
bio: Marie Gluesenkamp Perez has represented Washington's 3rd District since 2023 and is a leader in the Blue Dog Coalition. She previously co-owned an auto repair shop in Portland and served on the Underwood Conservation District board. She lives in Skamania County and studied economics at Reed College.

platform.point: Stop manufacturers from monopolizing repairs of farm equipment, vehicles and consumer goods.
Oppose a national abortion ban and protect women's access to doctors.
Fund police and firefighter retention to fight fentanyl and illegal guns.
Expand apprenticeships and extend Pell Grants to job training programs.
Pursue abundant, low-cost energy from both traditional and renewable sources to ease prices.
Rebuild American manufacturing and fix supply chains.

economy.evidence: Advocates reshoring manufacturing and skepticism of expanded free trade.

liberty.evidence: Supports abortion access (individual choice) but opposes an assault weapons ban while backing a higher gun purchase age, and voted for a 2026 gender-identity bill.

immigration.evidence: Voted for the Laken Riley Act and supported Title 42 expulsions and Remain in Mexico.

foreign.evidence: Co-sponsored a 2024 defense package with Ukraine aid and opposes conditions on aid to Israel.

energy.evidence: Accepts human-caused climate change but prioritizes cheap energy from both traditional and renewable sources.

tech.evidence: Co-introduced the REPAIR Act and SMART Act on right to repair.

education.evidence: Opposed Biden's student debt relief and promotes technical training alternatives to four-year degrees.

name: John Braun
current_role: Washington State Senator and Senate Republican Leader
bio: John Braun has represented the 20th District in the Washington State Senate since 2013 and has led the Senate Republican caucus, after earlier chairing the Ways and Means Committee. He is a retired Navy captain from the submarine force and president of Braun Northwest, an emergency vehicle manufacturer in Chehalis. He lives in Lewis County and studied at the University of Washington and the University of Michigan.

platform.point: Cut wasteful spending and reduce regulation on manufacturers and small businesses.
Finish barrier construction, hire agents, tighten asylum rules and target cartel supply chains.
Close open drug markets and pair camping bans with available shelter.
Give parents access to classroom information and lower college tuition.
Pursue market-based energy from hydropower, solar, oil, natural gas and nuclear.
Prioritize military readiness, veterans' care and domestic manufacturing capacity.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on spending cuts, lighter regulation and opposing tax increases.

liberty.evidence: Opposes gun restrictions (individual choice) but backs drug-market crackdowns and sex-based women's sports protections (community norms).

security.evidence: Supports expanded enforcement against drug markets and fentanyl interdiction.

immigration.evidence: Calls for completing border barriers and tightening asylum policy.

foreign.evidence: Emphasizes military readiness and naval defense strength.

energy.evidence: Backs an all-of-the-above approach including oil and natural gas.

education.evidence: Supports parental rights in schools while citing his record funding public education and cutting tuition.

notes: Whether he still holds the Senate Republican Leader post in September 2026 was not independently confirmed. The Commons image is a still from a YouTube video, so it was not used as a portrait.

name: Amanda McKinney
bio: Amanda McKinney is a Yakima County Commissioner from Central Washington and previously worked in banking. She serves on boards of the Washington State Association of Counties and the National Association of Counties and was appointed to the federal Wildland Fire Leadership Council.

platform.point: Secure the border to stop fentanyl trafficking and human smuggling.
Protect family farms and senior water rights and support the Yakima Basin Integrated Plan.
Support hydropower, natural gas and nuclear while opposing energy mandates.
Provide police with resources and back anti-crime efforts.
Oppose gun control measures, including fees and training requirements.
Root out fraud and wasteful spending and demand fiscal transparency.

liberty.evidence: Opposes gun restrictions (individual choice) but describes herself as pro-life and backs sex-based girls' sports rules (community norms).

security.evidence: Backs added resources for police and sheriff's offices.

immigration.evidence: Opposes open-border policies and emphasizes border security.

energy.evidence: Supported Initiative 2066 to repeal natural gas restrictions and opposes energy mandates.

tech.evidence: Favors U.S. tech leadership and opposes government control of cryptocurrency.

notes: Liberty raised from 45 to 55 because her campaign biography describes her as pro-life.

name: John Duresky
bio: John Duresky is a retired U.S. Air Force major who served three combat deployments. He spent 37 years in military and civil service, including work at the Hanford site, and lives in the Tri-Cities area of Central Washington.

platform.point: Remove trade tariffs, protect irrigation rights and reform the Farm Bill for small and mid-size farms.
Protect Hanford cleanup jobs, raise the federal minimum wage and reform the tax code.
Fund rural hospitals, restore ACA subsidies and work toward universal coverage.
Cut VA wait times and expand mental health care.
Adopt congressional term limits, ban member stock trading and overturn Citizens United.
Protect civil servants from politically motivated firings and strengthen whistleblower protections.

economy.evidence: Supports a higher federal minimum wage, union protections and tax code reform.

welfare.evidence: Seeks universal healthcare coverage and protecting Medicare and Medicaid.

immigration.evidence: Wants immigration policy aligned with farms' need for agricultural labor.

notes: The campaign image may be an outdoor photo rather than a formal headshot.

name: Michael Baumgartner
bio: Michael Baumgartner has represented Washington's 5th District since January 2025. He previously served as Spokane County Treasurer from 2019 to 2025 and as a state senator for the 6th District from 2011 to 2019, and earlier worked as a U.S. economics officer in Iraq and on counternarcotics in Afghanistan. He was born in Pullman and studied at Washington State University and Harvard.

platform.point: Curb federal spending to reduce inflation and the national debt.
Prioritize border security and enforcement of current immigration law.
Leave abortion law to each state.
Emphasize local control and parental choice in schools.
Support Eastern Washington farmers and protect the Lower Snake River dams.
Preserve promised Social Security and Medicare benefits without reductions.

economy.evidence: Opposes tax rate increases and supports eliminating the inheritance tax.

welfare.evidence: Has supported repealing Obamacare in favor of market-based insurance, while pledging to keep Social Security and Medicare benefits.

liberty.evidence: Opposes abortion and same-sex marriage (community norms) but has an NRA A rating and endorsed marijuana legalization (individual choice).

immigration.evidence: Opposed the DREAM Act and challenged Washington's sanctuary law in 2025.

foreign.evidence: Has called for ending foreign wars despite his service in Iraq and Afghanistan.

energy.evidence: Favors using abundant domestic energy supplies and questions human causes of climate change.

education.evidence: Supports parental choice and charter schools alongside public school investment.

faith.evidence: Supports letting Catholic health providers operate according to their religious values.

name: Carmela Conroy
bio: Carmela Conroy is a third-generation Eastern Washingtonian who served as a U.S. Foreign Service Officer across six administrations, with postings including Afghanistan, Japan, New Zealand, Norway and Pakistan. Earlier she was a deputy prosecutor in Spokane County.

platform.point: End tariff instability and normalize trade with Canada and Mexico.
Index the federal minimum wage to inflation and guarantee paid time off and sick leave.
Restore Medicare and Medicaid funding and extend Medicaid to all children through age 18.
Stop funding new detention centers and restore FEMA emergency funding.
Restore public education funding, including special education.
Ban congressional stock trading in favor of mutual funds.

economy.evidence: Supports an inflation-indexed minimum wage with mandated paid leave.

welfare.evidence: Wants Medicaid coverage for all children from birth to 18 and federal drug price negotiation.

liberty.evidence: Pledges to push for gun safety laws (guns); no stated positions found on other liberty issues.

immigration.evidence: Calls for defunding detention center construction.

foreign.evidence: Seeks to restore diplomatic and intelligence functions and uphold treaty commitments to allies.

education.evidence: Prioritizes restoring public education and special education funding.

faith.evidence: Wants to ensure public funds are not spent in violation of church-state separation.

notes: The foreign policy score rests on limited campaign language about diplomacy and allies.
